name: Moped
description: A motor vehicle with its power source built in and a seat, capable of no more than 30 mph with a 150-pound rider: either a bicycle-type vehicle with fully operative pedals and a motor equivalent to 130 cc or less, or an automatic motorcycle with a motor equivalent to 50 cc or less. An electric motor qualifies as an equivalent power unit, so an e-bike over 750 watts held to 30 mph lands here.

restrictions.rule: The power source is an integral part of the vehicle, with a seat for the operator; one with an added-on power unit is a motor bicycle instead

A bicycle-type vehicle with fully operative pedals and up to a 130 cc engine, or a motorcycle with an automatic transmission and up to a 50 cc engine, either size or an equivalent power unit; the motorcycle type needs no pedals
Capable of no more than 30 mph with a 150-pound rider on a dry, level, hard surface with no wind
Not a motor bicycle or an electric bicycle
Riders need a valid operator's license (a Class D license, not just an instruction permit) or a moped permit, which requires being 16 or older and having completed driver education
Titled and registered with the DMV
Allowed on any roadway except freeways or where mopeds are prohibited; in the right lane on roads with two or more lanes each way except to turn left
Not allowed on sidewalks, and not on a bicycle way with the power unit running
